notes: The tutorial covers many circuits (LED, button, buzzer, PIR, ultrasonic, MCP3008, motors); the supplied images show only the light-dependent-resistor circuit, so that is the circuit built here.

From the Fritzing image, the header pins used are pin 1 (3V3), pin 7 (GPIO4, matching LightSensor(4) in the code) and pin 6 (GND). The Pi is drawn rotated 180 degrees. I assumed raspberry-pi port 'GND.1' stands for GND pin 6.

The Fritzing image shows the breadboard with column 1 at the right. Wires are in row a of columns 1, 3 and 5. Component legs are in row e (the capacitor POS leg is placed in 3t.d in the same strip as 3t.e; it shares the column-3 strip, so it is electrically the same).

The LDR sits between column 1 (3V3) and column 3 (GPIO4). Only one LDR leg is clearly visible in the image, so the column-3 leg is inferred from the text ('capacitor in series with the LDR, positive leg on the same track as an LDR leg').
The capacitor POS leg is in column 3 (GPIO4 / LDR strip) and NEG in column 5 (GND), per the text. The catalogue's capacitor-10uf type was used for the 1uF capacitor, with value=1uF noted as a prop.
The photoresistor is symmetric, so which leg goes where is arbitrary.
Jumper wires are modelled as generic jumper-wire parts; the red, green and black colours come from the image.
